answer_summary: The 2.5 V electron energy is 241.2125 kJ mol^-1. Of the listed C-X BDEs, only C-I at 228 kJ mol^-1 is no greater than this energy, so the possible-halogen set is exactly {I}.
assumptions: Standard electrical-energy law E = qV; for one mole of singly charged electrons q = F, and 1 C V = 1 J.
As directed by the prompt's comparison of voltage with bond energies, a listed C-X bond passes the energetic screen exactly when its BDE is no greater than the available molar electron energy.
